title: Prepositions and patterns
summary: Learn common word patterns as whole phrases, and choose the preposition or verb form each one needs.

sections.title: Words that travel together
content: Some words almost always bring another word with them. In English we say ‘interested in’, not ‘interested on’. Indonesian may use a different pattern, so translation does not always help.
A rule rarely explains these pairs, so it is better to learn the whole phrase.

sections.title: Three patterns to look for
content: Verb and preposition: rely on, wait for, belong to. Adjective and preposition: good at, afraid of, proud of.
Verb and -ing or to: some verbs take -ing (enjoy reading, suggest going), and others take to (decide to go, hope to win).
After a preposition, a verb takes -ing: ‘good at swimming’, not ‘good at swim’.

sections.title: Work through an example
content: Take: ‘Ali is tired ___ waiting.’ The adjective tired pairs with of here, and after of the verb takes -ing.
Take: ‘They hope ___ the bridge soon.’ Hope is followed by to and the base verb, so ‘to finish’ fits.

sections.title: Find the word that controls the gap
content: Underline the word just before the gap. Ask which word usually follows it, and then choose.

sections.title: Check the form too
content: Some of these items test the preposition, and others test the verb form after a word. Read the sentence with your choice in place.

sections.title: Find where it went wrong
content: Pattern error: I had not learned this pair. Translation error: I copied the pattern from another language. Form error: I used the right pair, but the wrong verb form after it.
Write the whole phrase in your notebook with a new example, not only the small word.

sections.title: Try a new text
content: Complete one unseen short text with three gaps. If you need a hint or get it wrong, you will try a new text with different patterns.
